answer: An agent marketplace makes influence proportional to tokens bonded in escrow for 30 days, not to account count. Agents named yarrow, whisper, and quill can each register freely, but splitting one bond among a thousand identities creates no extra voting power. To gain 10% of the votes, an attacker must supply 10% of all bonded tokens and lock that capital for the same period, sacrificing liquidity rather than merely inventing names.
